---
title: "Preface"
---

::: {.lead}
This documentation explains how to use [SysNDD](https://sysndd.dbmr.unibe.ch/){.no-external}, an expert-curated database of gene-disease associations in neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). It covers looking up genes, building gene panels, using the data programmatically, and curating records.
:::

## How this documentation is organized {.unnumbered}

- **Getting started** explains the entity concept and the evidence categories.
- **Using SysNDD** covers the public web app, the API and your account. Only signing in needs an account.
- **Curation** holds the rules: the curation criteria, how to research a gene, and the re-review instructions for Reviewers.
- **Curator guide** covers the workflows for Curators and Administrators.
- **Reference** describes the data model and terms, and how to cite SysNDD.
- **For developers** covers local development and deployment.

Chapters that describe a task start with a **Who can do this** box. It names the lowest role that can do the task: public (no account), Reviewer, Curator or Administrator.

## How to cite {.unnumbered}

If you use SysNDD, cite the preprint [@popp_sysndd_2026]. If you refer to the predecessor database SysID, also cite the original publication [@kochinke_systematic_2016]. [Cite SysNDD and reuse its data](reference-citing.qmd) explains how to cite the data, including a specific data release once one is published, and the data license.

## Get help {.unnumbered}

Write to support [at] sysndd.org for questions about the data, problems with the site, or feature requests. [Report a problem](02-web-tool.qmd#report-a-problem) lists what to include in a problem report.

## History of SysID and SysNDD {.unnumbered}

SysNDD grew out of SysID, conceived by Annette Schenck and Christiane Zweier in 2009 and published in 2016 [@kochinke_systematic_2016]. Christiane Zweier has been involved in SysID from its start and has performed and coordinated its curation and updates since.

The SysID web tool was written in PHP. After its first release it received only necessary bug fixes. When the hosting agreement at the CMBI at Radboud University in Nijmegen ended, SysID moved to a server at the Department for BioMedical Research (DBMR) at the University of Bern. The original link from the 2016 publication still redirects there. The legacy code is archived in a [GitHub repository (SysID)](https://github.com/berntpopp/SysID). SysID now shows a notice that its content is no longer curated.

In 2019 the SysID curation effort began working with Orphanet, supported by the European Reference Network ITHACA (ERN ITHACA). Aligning gene, disease and phenotype naming with Orphanet led to a new database design and web app: SysNDD. Bernt Popp (Institute of Human Genetics, University Hospital Leipzig) designed and built the SysNDD software.
